mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and higher corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following low UNRATE, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% indicates monetary easing, which may stimulate economic activity and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive returns in more than 60% of the 20-day windows after FEDFUNDS drops below 0.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases and payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases, it signals a strong labor market, which may lead to higher consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following simultaneous improvements in UNRATE and PAYEMS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic demand, which may lead to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show positive returns in more than 50% of the 60-day windows following GDP growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong supply activity, which may lead to increased economic output and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following an increase in INDPRO, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A high consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicates inflationary pressures, which may lead to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show negative returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows following high CPIAUCSL, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is low and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is high, it indicates a sluggish economy that may require monetary stimulus, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following the joint condition of low FEDFUNDS and high UNRATE, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) indicates weak demand in the housing market, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 does not show negative returns in more than 50% of the 60-day windows following a decline in HOUST, the hypothesis is rejected.
